---
name: checkpoint
description: End-of-session SeamSpec check. Verifies the locked rules, proposes rules for behavior built this session, and records approaches that failed and design decisions made. Use when the user says "wrap up", "checkpoint" or "before I commit".
argument-hint: "[area to focus on]"
---
<!-- Generated by seamspec from template "checkpoint". Edit seamspec/templates/commands/checkpoint.md and run `python -m seamspec.core.commands`. -->

Run a SeamSpec checkpoint for this session. Optional focus: $ARGUMENTS

1. Call `verify(scope="all")`. If it reports `not_permitted`, run `seamspec verify` with your
   shell tool instead (the user may be asked to allow it). If any LOCKED rule fails, stop here:
   fix the regression, or, if the change is intentional, follow the supersede steps
   (`/seamspec:supersede`).
2. List the files changed this session: `git diff --name-only HEAD`, plus untracked files.
3. Call `get_constraints` on them, so you don't propose a rule that already exists.
4. If the project keeps a list of rules it intends to lock (for example a section of its
   plan), start with the ones whose code now exists and works. Then pick behaviors
   established this session that are worth protecting. At most 3 in total (fewer is fine;
   if `.seamspec/config.toml` sets `commands.max_proposals_per_run`, use that limit): explicit
   user constraints, user-visible behavior, security, data integrity. Skip cosmetic or trivial
   behavior. Propose each with `propose_invariant`, then run `seamspec verify --proposed <id>`.
5. Record every approach tried and abandoned this session with `log_dead_end`.
6. Record design choices settled this session that shape future work on specific files (for
   example deferring a feature after measuring it, choosing an algorithm or a data
   representation, or setting a module boundary) with `propose_decision`, scoped to those files.
   Only a rationale or trade-off belongs here: something a test can check is a rule (step 4), and
   a failed attempt is a dead end (step 5). Skip choices `get_constraints` already shows.
   Decisions count toward the same limit as the rules in step 4 (rules and decisions together);
   if it's reached, list the choices you didn't record and say so.

---
Rules for every SeamSpec command:
- Never approve invariants and never edit files under `.seamspec/` directly.
- `propose_invariant` never runs tests. After proposing, run `seamspec verify --proposed <id>`
  (repeat `--proposed <id>` for each id) with your shell tool; the user may be asked to allow it.
  Never try to work around that prompt.
- If SeamSpec MCP tools are unavailable, use the CLI instead: `seamspec context <files>`,
  `seamspec propose --json -`, `seamspec dead-end --json -`, `seamspec propose-decision --json -`,
  `seamspec verify --json`.
- End your reply with the SeamSpec summary block:

  SeamSpec · <command>
  ✅ <created or passed items, with ids>
  ⏭  <dismissed or skipped items>
  ⚠️ <failures or items needing attention>
  Next: <one action for the user, e.g. "run `seamspec review` (3 pending)">
